 Brook's Historic Double Ton in Vain as Sri Lanka Pull Off Stunning Chase
 23/10/2026 06:49 Harry Brook produced England's first ODI double century, but even that was not enough to stop Sri Lanka from completing a breathtaking two-wicket victory in a record-breaking run fest in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
 Harry Brook celebrates his double ton. @ECB Chasing 430, Sri Lanka overcame an early wobble and a dramatic final-over collapse to reach 430 for eight with one ball remaining, pulling off the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.
 Pavan Rathnayake's career-best 130 laid the foundation, while Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka struck 97 apiece before Janith Liyanage's unbeaten 61 delivered the finishing blow.
 Brook's Masterclass Sets Up Imposing Total
 Earlier, Brook had threatened to make the contest a one-man show with a sensational 202 off 114 balls.
 After a cautious start, the England captain unleashed an astonishing range of strokes, reaching his century off 75 balls before needing just 39 more deliveries for his second hundred.
 Joe Root contributed 69 and Will Jacks an unbeaten 66 as England piled up 429 for four, plundering 156 runs from the final 10 overs.
 Brook became the first England batter to score an ODI double century, but the landmark offered little consolation.
 It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes.
 Brook admitted
 Rathnayake And Shanaka Turn The Tide
 Sri Lanka's chase looked in serious trouble at 24 for two before Rathnayake and Avishka revived their hopes with a 166-run partnership.
 Avishka fell three short of a century, but Shanaka's promotion up the order proved inspired.
 Pavan Rathnayake shines with bat. @OfficialSLC The former captain hammered eight sixes in his 50-ball 97, adding 133 with Rathnayake to keep Sri Lanka within striking distance. Rathnayake, named Player of the Match, credited the collective effort.
 We thought it was a good wicket, backed our normal game. It was a good team effort. Every partnership was important," he said.
 Rathnayake
 Liyanage Holds Nerve In Frantic Finish
 Sri Lanka still needed 107 from 58 balls when Liyanage arrived. He attacked relentlessly, striking seven fours and three sixes.
 Josh Tongue briefly revived England's hopes by dismissing Dunith Wellalage and Eshan Malinga off successive deliveries in the final over.
 But Asitha Fernando survived the hat-trick ball and returned the strike to Liyanage, who launched Tongue over long-off to settle the contest.
 Captain Kusal Mendis hailed his team's belief. "Everyone believed we can do it. Everyday we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score," he said.
 Brook conceded England had been outplayed. "Incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional. Sri Lanka just outplayed us," he said.
 Brief Scores: England 429/4 (Harry Brook 202, Joe Root 69, Will Jacks 66\*, Tom Banton 50) lost to Sri Lanka 430/8 (Pavan Rathnayake 130, Avishka Fernando 97, Dasun Shanaka 97, Janith Liyanage 61\*; Josh Tongue 3/79) by two wickets.
